translation.text: And I came into the garden of righteousness, and I saw many large trees growing there [an expression concerning those trees remains unresolved].[a] Two of them were beautiful and great, their beauty abundant, and they were glorious; and the tree of wisdom,[b] from which those who eat know great wisdom.

footnotes.text: Not ready for application: the selected expression ከሐክቲሆሙ and its construction remain unresolved. Actual primary Dillmann1865 column824 explicitly cites this unit, calls the word obscure and doubtful, and only tentatively discusses multicoloured mixture or variety. It does not establish a spatial-preposition meaning. The modern bracketed English label is not a recovered ancient clause and does not choose among, beside or beyond from the facing Greek, nor adopt the lexicon’s tentative suggestion. The selected numeral ፪ in ፪እሙ, two of them, is separately visible; it is not a fragrance noun or a Greek import.

The singular tree of wisdom and the eating/knowing-wisdom relationship are retained. No missing tree-of-life phrase is supplied from an editor’s discussion, no numeral two is converted into two different named trees, and no complete Genesis wording is inserted.

transcription_uncertainties.description: Selected comparison glyphs retained, lexical/construction meaning genuinely unresolved. New English preserves the expression untranslated as ḥamara ṣərāʾ rather than supplying a guessed species or a fake full gloss. This is proposed critical treatment, not lexical resolution or independent approval.

translation.text: And it resembled ḥamara ṣərāʾ,[a] and its fruit was like a cluster of grapes, very beautiful[b]; and the fragrance of that tree spread far away.

footnotes.text: Ḥamara ṣərāʾ retains the selected expression ሐመረ፡ ጽራእ untranslated in transliteration because its complete meaning is unresolved. Actual primary Dillmann1865 column76 discusses this compound and explicitly cites32:4; column1275 calls its second element uncertain and questions whether it is a tree name or a form related to a name for Greece. Those discussions do not establish pine, carob, tamarind, cherry, a modern species or one secure English gloss. This is an explicitly provisional critical treatment, not a claim that the lexical problem is solved. No different-edition reading or Greek height/leaf clause is silently supplied.

The selected fruit comparison uses the vine-cluster expression. The correct primary cross-reference is column752 to378, where the noun has collective and singular uses with plural forms separately listed. “A cluster of grapes” is a bounded rendering of that range, not a claim that the passage counts exactly one cluster. An earlier95 locator was a neighbouring-entry error and is not positive lexical proof. The selected good/beautiful expression is rendered once; no Greek leaf-comparison clause is added.

translation.text: And I said, “This tree is beautiful, and how [beautiful and] delightful its appearance is!”[a]

footnotes.text: The selected edited Geʽez brackets “beautiful and” in the second clause; Charles 1906 printed p74 note2 recommends omitting those words with G and q. Fresh inspection reads the selected tree form ዕፀ at the beginning of PDF112 and the bracketed adjective ሠናይ against the same selected font elsewhere in the unit/page; the source is not normalized to another edition. translation.text: Then Raphael, the holy angel who was with me, answered me and said to me, “This is the tree of wisdom from which your aged father and your mother ate—your ancestors who preceded you. They knew wisdom, their eyes were opened, they knew that they were naked, and they were driven from the garden.”[a]

footnotes.text: The complete selected Ethiopic unit is printed before XXXIII. It has a singular aged father and a singular mother, followed by the plural ancestral expression አበዋቲከ፡ እለ፡ ቀደሙከ. “Your ancestors who preceded you” is a bounded, explicitly provisional apposition to those two people, not a replacement by Adam and Eve or an invented additional group. The actual longer ancestral word corrects an earlier shortened draft transcription; the primary father entry permits plural parents and forebears. The selected plural opened-eyes, knowing, nakedness and expulsion clauses remain Ethiopic text, without a supplied agent. The facing Greek gives only the short father/eating clause followed by editorial dots; it does not attest the entire Ethiopic unit, and its dots do not mark a missing Ethiopic ending. Dillmann1851 was used only as an aligned edited-Geʽez comparison, not to replace Charles’s selected word order or claim fresh manuscripts.
